tool.name: DotMatch CRISPR count
tool.description: count guides from known-target FASTQ reads
tool.command:
#import re
#set $indel_args = "" #if str($metric) == 'levenshtein' and int($indel_window) > 0 #set $indel_args = "--indel-window '" + str($indel_window) + "'" #end if
printf 'sample_id\tfastq\n' > samples.tsv && #for $sample in $reads: #set $sample_label = re.sub(r'(?i)\.(?:fastq|fastqsanger)(?:\.gz)?$', '', str($sample.element_identifier)) #set $sample_id = re.sub(r'[^\w.-]', '_', str($sample_label)) #if $sample.is_of_type('fastq.gz', 'fastqsanger.gz'): #set $fastq_name = $sample_id + '.fastq.gz' #else: #set $fastq_name = $sample_id + '.fastq' #end if ln -s '$sample' '$fastq_name' && printf '%s\t%s\n' '$sample_id' '$fastq_name' >> samples.tsv && #end for dotmatch crispr-count --library '$library' --samples samples.tsv --guide-start '$guide_start' --guide-length '$guide_length' --k '$k' --metric '$metric' --ambiguity-policy radius $indel_args --out '$counts' --summary '$summary' --sample-qc '$sample_qc' --ambiguous '$ambiguous' --no-progress

param.name: library
param.label: Guide library
param.help: MAGeCK-style CSV or target TSV accepted by DotMatch.

param.name: reads
param.label: CRISPR guide FASTQ reads
param.help: Provide one FASTQ dataset per sample. Galaxy dataset names become sample IDs in the count and QC outputs.

param.name: guide_start
param.label: Guide start
param.help: Zero-based start position of the guide window in each read.

param.name: indel_window
param.label: Levenshtein indel window
param.help: Used only with the Levenshtein metric.

param.name: ambiguous
param.label: Ambiguous read handling
param.option: Keep ambiguity diagnostics in the run outputs

tool.help:
**What it does**
DotMatch counts CRISPR guide reads against a supplied known guide library. It writes a MAGeCK-compatible count table together with a JSON run summary and a per-sample QC table.
**Inputs**
Provide a guide library and one or more single-end FASTQ datasets. The Galaxy dataset names are used as sample IDs in the output count matrix and QC table. Set the zero-based guide start and guide length to the fixed read window used by the assay.
**Assignment and QC**
The wrapper keeps the radius ambiguity policy explicit. Unique, ambiguous, unmatched, and invalid read outcomes remain visible in the run summary and sample QC table. The count table can be passed to an appropriate downstream screen-analysis workflow; DotMatch does not perform gene-level statistical testing.
